All endpoints operate on servers y
ou have already added to a project in the\nhosted inspector. Managing API keys remains UI-only — see\n[Not in the API yet](#not-in

-the-api-yet).

## Base URL

```text theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1
```

The API is pat

h-versioned. All routes on this page are relative to the base
URL above.

## Authentication

Every request needs an MCPJam AP

I key in the `Authorization` header:

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
curl -X POST \
 "https://app.mcpjam.com/a
pi/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/servers/$SERVER_ID/tools\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY\" \\\n -H \"Content-Type:

application/json" \
 -d '{}'
```

### Creating a key

1. Open [**Settings → API keys**](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/a

pi-keys)
 in the hosted app (the card at the top of this page takes you there
 directly).
2. Click **Create API key**, name
it, and pick the **organization** it will act in.\n3. Copy the key (`sk_…`) immediately — **it is shown exactly once** and never\

n stored by MCPJam in retrievable form.

Keys can be revoked from the same page at any time. Revocation takes effect
immediat

ely.

### Scope

A key is bound to one MCPJam organization at creation and acts **as you,
inside that organization**. Per-req
uest authorization still applies: a call\nonly succeeds if the key's owner can access that project and server. A key\ncan never re

ach projects outside its organization.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Two deliberate restrictions while in preview:
>
> * **API keys cannot
manage API keys.** Requests to the key-management surface\n> with an `sk_…` bearer fail with `403 FORBIDDEN`. Create and revoke

keys in
> the UI.
> * **Guest sessions cannot use the API.** Sign in to create keys.

### Keep keys secret

Treat an API k

ey like a password:

* Load it from an environment variable or secret manager — never commit it to
 source control or ship it
in client-side code.\n* Scope keys narrowly: one key per integration, named so you can tell them apart.\n* Rotate by creating a re
placement key, switching traffic, then revoking the old one.\n* If a key leaks, revoke it immediately in\n [**Settings → API keys

**](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys).

If you see `401 UNAUTHORIZED` with `details.reason: "ORPHANED_KEY"`, the key
is no longer bound to an organization and cannot be used — create a new key\nfrom [Settings](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-k

eys).

## Conventions

**Requests.** Operations on servers are `POST` with a JSON body (most accept
an empty `{}`). **Reads**
— the catalog listings and eval-run polling — are\n`GET` and take their options (`cursor`, `limit`, filters) as query\nparameters

.

**Responses.** Three envelope shapes, used consistently:

| Kind | Shape |
| - | - |
| Single resource | The resource obj
ect directly |\n| Collection | `{ \"items\": [...], \"nextCursor\": \"...\" }` — `nextCursor` omitted on the last page |\n| Error
| `{ \"code\": \"...\", \"message\": \"...\", \"details\": {...} }` with a matching HTTP status |\n\n**Pagination.** Collections a
re cursor-based. Pass the previous response's\n`nextCursor` as `cursor` in the next request (body field on `POST` lists,\nquery pa
rameter on `GET` lists). Cursors are opaque — don't parse them.\n\n**Authoring vs running suites.** `POST /eval-suites` creates a
runnable suite\n(the suite plus its test cases) **synchronously** and responds `201` with the\n`suiteId`, WITHOUT running anything
— author once, run later. `POST /eval-runs`\nis the async counterpart: it validates and creates a run synchronously, then\ndetach
es execution and responds `202` with a `runId`. Poll\n`GET /eval-runs/{runId}` until `status` is `completed`, `failed`,\n`cancelle

d`, or `timed_out`.

**IDs.** Every identifier the API takes is discoverable through the API
itself: `GET /projects` lists your
projects, `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers`\nlists each project's servers, and `GET /projects/{projectId}/eval-suites`\nlists i

ts eval suites. Start from `GET /me` to confirm which account a key
acts as.

## Errors

Errors always use the canonical body
`{ code, message, details? }`. The `code`\nis stable and machine-readable; `message` is human-readable and may change;\n`details`

is an optional, unstructured bag.

| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
| - | - | - |
| `UNAUTHORIZED` | 401 | Missing, invalid, revoked
, or orphaned key |\n| `OAUTH_REQUIRED` | 401 | The **target MCP server** needs an OAuth grant — distinct from a bad key |\n| `AUT
H_REQUIRED` | 403 | The **target MCP server** allowed the connection and asked for sign-in on this call. `details.authChallenge` c
arries the parsed challenge. Your key is fine — see [Sign-in challenges](#sign-in-challenges) |\n| `FORBIDDEN` | 403 | Key is vali
d but not allowed to do this — or the **target MCP server** rejected the credentials MCPJam presented (retrying with a different M
CPJam key will not help; reconnect or re-authorize the server) |\n| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 | Malformed body or parameters |\n| `
NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Unknown project, server, or resource |\n| `CONFLICT` | 409 | The resource isn't in a state that accepts this wr
ite — a stale `expectedRevision`, a duplicate name, or an environment that can't currently be launched. Re-read and retry |\n| `FE
ATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED` | 422 | The target server doesn't support this MCP capability |\n| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | Too many requests —
see [Rate limits](#rate-limits) |\n| `SERVER_UNREACHABLE` | 502 | Could not connect to the target MCP server |\n| `TIMEOUT` | 504

| The target MCP server connected but didn't respond in time |
| `INTERNAL_ERROR` | 500 | Something failed on our side |

New

error codes may be **added** over time; treat unknown codes as
non-retryable failures unless the HTTP status says otherwise.

#

## Sign-in challenges

Some MCP servers allow the connection and ask for sign-in only on a protected
call. The API never starts

a sign-in. It reports the challenge instead:

* **HTTP 401 from the MCP server** on `tools/call`: the API answers
 `403 AUTH_
REQUIRED`. `details.authChallenge` carries the parsed challenge:\n its `source` (`http_401`), and the `error`, `requiredScope`, a
nd\n `resourceMetadataUrl` the server sent, when present.\n* **An `isError` result carrying `_meta[\"mcp/www_authenticate\"]`** (
the\n ChatGPT convention): the call succeeds, and the `CallToolResult` is returned\n unchanged with an additive `authChallenge`

field (`source:
 "tool_result_meta"`). A field the server already set under that name is never
 overwritten.

`AUTH_REQUIR
ED` is not `UNAUTHORIZED`: your MCPJam key is fine, so a different\nkey will not help. Complete the OAuth flow for that server you
rself, upload the\ntoken to one of its [accounts](#server-accounts), and call again. See\n[Mid-session sign-in](https://docs.mcpja

m.com/inspector/lazy-authentication.md).

## Rate limits

Each key gets **60 requests per minute** sustained, with bursts up t

o **10**.
Exceeding it returns `429 RATE_LIMITED` with a `Retry-After` header (in
seconds):

```http theme={"theme":"css-va

riables"}
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 7

{ "code": "RATE_LIMITED", "message": "API key rate limit exce
